units.title: Read the board
units.goal: Recognize a legal special move and check what it changes.

exercises.question: Which move brings the king and rook into play together?
exercises.explanation: Castling moves the king and rook together. Before doing it, inspect the squares the king crosses.

exercises.question: Which promotion ends the game immediately?
exercises.explanation: Look at the king’s escapes before choosing a promotion. More than one piece can end this game immediately.

units.title: Get out of check
units.goal: Trace the checking line and find a legal evasion before looking for threats.

exercises.question: Which square lets the king leave both attacks?
exercises.explanation: Two different pieces are giving check here. Trace both attacks before choosing a destination for the king.

exercises.question: Which king move avoids offering the queen to the rook?
exercises.explanation: Compare moving the king with blocking on the rook’s file. Count the pieces lost in any capture and recapture.

units.title: Count the cost of a capture
units.goal: Check attackers, defenders and the order of exchanges.

exercises.question: Which capture works once you follow the reply as well?
exercises.explanation: Compare the material before and after the full sequence. The first capture alone does not tell you how the exchange ends.

exercises.question: Which capture leaves you ahead after the opponent answers?
exercises.explanation: Identify what the opponent can take back before choosing the capture. Check the result on the board after their reply.

units.title: See the opponent’s next threat
units.goal: Scan the opponent’s immediate threat before choosing your own move.

exercises.question: Which response deals with the most urgent danger?
exercises.explanation: Start by checking what the opponent can do on their very next move. Compare the available defensive replies.

exercises.question: What can you change before the opponent continues their attack?
exercises.explanation: Try both an active reply and a direct defence in your head. Then test which one holds up on this board.

units.title: Deliver a simple mate
units.goal: Check the king’s escape squares, possible captures and blocks.

exercises.question: Which move ends the game by covering the king’s remaining exits?
exercises.explanation: After giving check, count the king’s usable squares and test whether another piece can capture or block.

exercises.question: Which first check lets you cover the king’s remaining exits on the next move?
exercises.explanation: Look one reply ahead. Make sure the king has no safe escape after your follow-up.

units.title: Develop with a purpose
units.goal: Develop a piece or support the centre while keeping the king safe.

exercises.question: Which move improves your opening position while keeping the king safe?
exercises.explanation: Compare moves that support the centre with castling. Several plans can be sound at this stage.

exercises.question: Which move helps a piece take on a useful job?
exercises.explanation: Compare which pieces can become more useful before you start forcing exchanges.

units.title: Recognize a mating pattern
units.goal: Spot the back-rank pattern and account for escape squares.

exercises.question: Which move takes advantage of the king’s lack of an exit?
exercises.explanation: Check whether a pawn or piece blocks the king’s escape before trying the back-rank pattern.

exercises.question: Where can the king escape after your first check?
exercises.explanation: Consider the pieces that can intervene and the squares they stop the king from reaching.

units.title: Attack two targets
units.goal: Find a move or preparation that attacks two targets.

exercises.question: Which move sets up threats against two targets?
exercises.explanation: Name both targets before you play, then check which one survives the strongest reply.

exercises.question: Which checks could change which pieces are available to attack?
exercises.explanation: Watch how the targets change after the opponent answers a check.

units.title: Exploit or escape a line tactic
units.goal: Trace the piece in front and the more valuable target behind it.

exercises.question: Which move takes advantage of the defender’s limited movement?
exercises.explanation: Trace the attack along the line and check whether the front piece can legally respond.

exercises.question: What becomes exposed when the first target moves?
exercises.explanation: Follow the attack through the front target and see what is left behind it.

units.title: Open an attack line
units.goal: Notice the piece that becomes active when another moves out of its way.

exercises.question: Which move opens a line while creating a second problem?
exercises.explanation: Look behind the moving piece. Check what the piece on the opened line can attack.

exercises.question: Which move can let two pieces attack the king at once?
exercises.explanation: Trace the new attack from the moving piece and the attack it uncovers.

units.title: Race a passed pawn
units.goal: Count promotion moves and account for the opponent’s checks and king route.

exercises.question: Which move gives your pawn the best head start?
exercises.explanation: Count each pawn’s moves to promotion. Check whether the opposing king can get into the pawn’s path.

exercises.question: Which first move changes the outcome of the pawn race?
exercises.explanation: Count the promotion moves for both players and look for checks that interrupt either race.

units.title: Look one reply deeper
units.goal: Compare tempting moves against the opponent’s strongest response.

exercises.question: Which check changes the order of threats after the reply?
exercises.explanation: Follow the checks and promotion in order. Stop only after you have looked at the opponent’s next reply.

exercises.question: What can you improve before making a forcing move?
exercises.explanation: Compare a preparatory move with the tempting immediate check. Give the opponent a chance to reply to both.

units.title: Change what the defender can do
units.goal: Move, remove or distract a defender before acting on the target it protects.

exercises.question: What could make a defender leave its current job?
exercises.explanation: Watch what stops being protected after the defending piece changes squares.

exercises.question: Which move draws a piece onto a square where you can use it as a target?
exercises.explanation: Follow where the defender lands and test your next move from that new position.

units.title: Decide whether a sacrifice works
units.goal: Compare taking the offer with declining it and identify the concrete payoff.

exercises.question: What could change around the king if the opponent accepts the capture?
exercises.explanation: Count what you offer, then see what the sequence gains. Consider a reply that declines the offer too.

exercises.question: Which reply would you check before offering material?
exercises.explanation: Follow the opponent’s strongest response before deciding whether the material is worth offering.

units.title: Win or hold a pawn ending
units.goal: Use king position and tempo to steer a pawn ending.

exercises.question: Which king move keeps you in front of your pawn?
exercises.explanation: Compare the king routes and count whose turn it will be when the kings face each other.

exercises.question: Which king route gives your pawn the best chance to advance?
exercises.explanation: Check the king’s path before pushing. In a pawn ending a single tempo can change which squares you can reach.

units.title: Convert material and choose trades
units.goal: Compare what remains after an exchange against keeping the pieces.

exercises.question: Which capture leaves you with the simplest position to finish?
exercises.explanation: After each candidate, identify exactly which pieces remain. A simple capture can leave the opponent with far fewer resources.

exercises.question: Which continuation makes your advantage easier to use?
exercises.explanation: Compare simplifying with keeping pieces. Play out the opponent’s reply before deciding which position you prefer.

units.title: Activate the least useful piece
units.goal: Find a practical destination and compare how the opponent can respond.

exercises.question: Which move helps development or challenges the centre?
exercises.explanation: Compare which pieces can join the game and what each candidate does to the contested squares.

exercises.question: Which quiet move helps you prepare before making a direct threat?
exercises.explanation: Look for a way to improve the position before starting a forcing line. Compare the next useful move after each candidate.

units.title: Read pawn structure and choose a break
units.goal: Find the contact point and check what opens when pawns exchange.

exercises.question: Which pawn move challenges the centre from the side?
exercises.explanation: Compare the break with leaving the pawn chain intact. Trace which lines open after an exchange.

exercises.question: Which pawn move changes the central tension now?
exercises.explanation: Look for a pawn you can challenge and note what would become available to each side if they trade.

units.title: Attack or defend the king with a plan
units.goal: Compare the king’s exits and the number of useful attacking pieces.

exercises.question: Which move makes it hardest for the king to escape?
exercises.explanation: Map the exits and the pieces that cover them. Check how the opponent can interpose or take.

exercises.question: What can you play to leave the king with fewer safe squares?
exercises.explanation: After your move, check the king’s available exits and trace what your queen controls on the new square.

units.title: Convert or defend a rook ending
units.goal: Compare rook activity, king placement and passed-pawn progress.

exercises.question: Which move makes the passed pawn harder to stop?
exercises.explanation: Before giving check, compare what your rook and king can do to help the pawn advance.

exercises.question: Where can your rook become active without ignoring the pawns?
exercises.explanation: Compare checks from a distance with moving behind the pawn. Follow the reply before committing.

units.title: Recognize a familiar opening structure
units.goal: Recognize the pawn structure and compare moves that fit it.

exercises.question: Which move fits the pawn structure you have reached?
exercises.explanation: Compare the pieces that need developing and the central tension. The structure matters even when the move order changes.

exercises.question: Which move fits this centre while keeping development flexible?
exercises.explanation: Compare how each candidate changes the centre or helps a piece develop. Look for the opponent’s likely pawn break.
